name: table-errors
body:
A table violation uses the validation error format (error-reporting): file, line, path, message and a fix. The line points into the table — at the offending row, at the delimiter row for a header/delimiter mismatch, or at the table's own first line for a whole-table limit — and is file-absolute. The path names the table position within the body (for example `body` for a whole-table limit, and the offending row or cell within it), so a strict-column-count violation reads `rows[2]: 3 cells, header has 4` at that row's line and an unknown-attribute violation carries the closest-match suggestion (closest-match-suggestions). A table violation is reported with the same text in terminal and browser (whole-deck-validation), through `kalide check` (cli-check) and `kalide start` (cli-start).

AC: a strict-column-count error names the row and both counts with its line on the offending row; a limit error names the limit and the actual count; an unknown-attribute error carries the closest-match suggestion; a header/delimiter mismatch is positioned on the delimiter row; the same error text appears in the terminal and in the browser error page.
